title: French dioceses A (batch 4): bounded original-book states and dated Roman-rite changes

traditions.label: Évreux diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1740 Paris printing of the Missale Ebroicense issued under Pierre-Jules-César de Rochechouart, as offered by Numelyo from Lyon SJ LB 030/80.
traditions.coverage_note: One printing, its complete pastoral mandate and selected original loci are directly inspected; predecessor editions, later revisions, actual local uptake and complete text remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Lodève diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1776 Paris printing of the Missale Lodovense issued under Jean-Félix-Henri de Fumel, as offered by Numelyo from Lyon 31754.
traditions.coverage_note: One printing, its complete pastoral letter and the Canon opening are directly inspected; the 1511 edition, the earlier local missal named in the letter, actual uptake and complete text remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Le Puy diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1543 Lyon printing of the Missale ad usum Aniciensis ecclesiae, sold at Le Puy by Jean Allard, as offered by Numelyo from Lyon Rés 129080.
traditions.coverage_note: One pre-Tridentine printing is directly inspected at title, colophon and Canon; its relation to the 1511 and 1527 editions, later reform and complete text remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Autun diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1831 Missale Aeduense of Bishop du Trousset d'Héricourt and the 1858 Autun proper Masses for use with the Roman Missal, both as offered by Google Books from Lyon copies.
traditions.coverage_note: Two bounded publication states are directly inspected: a diocesan missal and, after the return to the Roman liturgy, an approved diocesan proper. Earlier editions, the Roman Missal edition used and complete texts remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Chalon-sur-Saône diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1765 Paris printing of the Missale Cabillonense issued under Louis-Henri de Rochefort d'Ally, as offered by Google Books from a Lyon copy.
traditions.coverage_note: One printing, its mandate and the Canon opening are directly inspected; the date conflict with the 1767 catalogue record, earlier editions, uptake and complete text remain unresolved.

traditions.label: Couserans diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1753 Paris printing of the Missale Conseranense issued under Joseph de Saint-André Marnais de Verceil, as offered by Tolosana from BU Toulouse Res 1335.
traditions.coverage_note: One printing, its complete letter and the Canon opening are directly inspected; earlier books, uptake and complete text remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Albi diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1766 Paris printing of the Missale Albiense issued under Léopold-Charles de Choiseul, as offered by Tolosana from BU Toulouse Res 1341.
traditions.coverage_note: One printing, its letter and the Canon opening are directly inspected; the relation to the 1764 record, the 1846 edition, uptake and complete text remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Luçon diocesan Mass books
traditions.scope: The 1891 approved proper of Masses for the diocese of Luçon, used with the Roman Missal, as offered by Google Books from a Harvard copy.
traditions.coverage_note: One approved Roman-rite diocesan proper is directly inspected; the eighteenth- and nineteenth-century diocesan missals, the date of the Roman adoption and complete texts remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Elne (Perpignan) diocesan Mass books
traditions.scope: The 1847 episcopal mandate imposing the Roman Missal with a diocesan proper for the diocese of Elne (seat at Perpignan), printed in its Officia propria.
traditions.coverage_note: A dated primary act of Roman-Missal adoption is directly inspected; the medieval printings (1506, 1511), the Roman Missal edition used and the diocesan proper's Mass texts remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Angers diocesan Mass books
traditions.scope: The SRC approval of 17 June 1857 of the Angers calendar and proper of Offices and Masses for the return to the Roman liturgy, as reprinted in the 1881 Angers Officia propria.
traditions.coverage_note: A dated primary approval of a Roman-rite diocesan proper is directly inspected; the medieval and neo-Gallican Angers missals and the proper's Mass texts remain unestablished.

traditions.label: Bayonne diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1543 (completed January 1544 new style) Paris printing of a missal for Bayonne ordered by Bishop Étienne Poncher, as described in detail by Dubarat (1891) from the unique Mazarine copy.
traditions.coverage_note: One sixteenth-century state is documented from an inspected scholarly description, not from the original; the 1753 and 1836 editions, the 1858 return to the Roman liturgy and complete text remain unestablished.

sources.title: Officia propria ad usum dioecesis Elnensis (Perpignan, J.-B. Alzine, 1847), copy digitized by Google
sources.inspection: Google Books full view. Directly viewed: mandate pages PR7 and PR8 (printed pp. vii–viii): all archdeacons, canons, archpriests, deans, parish priests, vicars, priests and clerics in sacred orders are to use the Roman Missal and Breviary together with this proper, in solemn and private celebration, from the next 1 January; other rites are forbidden and every other missal or breviary is declared prohibited after that date; dated Perpignan, episcopal palace, 1 November 1847 (All Saints), signed Joannes-Franciscus, bishop of Elne, countersigned Bédos. PR5–PR6 (earlier mandate pages on calendar ranks) read by OCR only.

sources.title: Officia propria ... Andegavensis, pars aestiva (1881), copy digitized by Google
sources.inspection: Google Books full view. Directly viewed: PT8 (printed p. 50): the SRC prefect approved the perpetual calendar and the Proprium Officiorum atque Missarum of the diocese of Angers with marginal corrections and granted that it be observed perpetually by the Angers clergy both in the canonical Hours according to the Roman rite and in the celebration of Masses; 17 June 1857; Cardinal Patrizi, prefect; H. Capalti, secretary; concordat signed by Charles-Émile, bishop of Angers. PT7 (the decree's narrative) was also directly viewed: Bishop Guillaume-Laurent-Louis Angebault, concerned to recall the Roman liturgy to his diocese, with chapter assent prepared a perpetual calendar and Offices and Masses from approved sources and submitted the printed calendar and Proprium Officiorum atque Missarum to Pius IX.

sources.title: Missale ad usum ecclesie cathedralis [Baionensis, misprinted Bajocensis] (Paris, Jean Kaerbriand alias Huguelin for Regnault Chaudière, 1543/1544), Mazarine 1162 B
sources.inspection: Victor Dubarat, Le bréviaire de Lescar de 1541 réédité avec une introduction et des notes sur nos anciennes liturgies locales (Pau, L. Ribaut, 1891), Google Books full view. Directly viewed: p. lxxxix (identification of the 1543/1544 Paris missal titled 'Bajocensis' as Bayonne's, Poncher's order, Mazarine 1162 B as unique copy, comparison with a 1545 Bayeux missal by the same printer); p. xc (physical description, transcribed title, printer Kaerbriand alias Huguelin for Regnault Chaudière, MDXLIII, two parts of 136 and 108 folios); p. xci (calendar, blessings, temporale incipit for the diocese of Bayonne, notated prefaces including a proper Palm Sunday preface, Canon with additions, sanctoral, common and votive Masses). Pages liv and cxcviii were also viewed or OCR-read for Lescar and the later Auch-province liturgy.
sources.limitations: A scholarly description, partly relying on Marais and Cazenave; the original Mazarine volume was not inspected. Dubarat's notes on later Bayonne liturgy (cxcviii ff.) were only partly acquired before Google refused further automated access.

stages.label: 1740 Évreux diocesan missal
stages.scope: The identified 1740 Évreux missal, its complete episcopal mandate, and selected original preface and Canon loci.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ebroicense, Paris 1740, Lyon SJ LB 030/80
stages.summary: The title names Bishop Pierre-Jules-César de Rochechouart and the cathedral chapter. His mandate, dated 18 April 1740, says the editors went back to the Ordo Romanus and ancient sacramentaries, drew many Secrets and Postcommunions from the recently edited Leonine Sacramentary, added prefaces for Advent, Corpus Christi and some feasts, took sung texts from Scripture, restricted sequences to solemn days, arranged ceremonies after the older Évreux form, and restored proper ferial epistles and gospels. It commands the diocese's churches, chapters, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities, confraternities and priests bound by law or custom to the Évreux Office to use this missal and no other.

evidence.claim: The book names Évreux, the bishop's authority with chapter consent, Paris, 1740 and the royal privilege.

evidence.locus: views 7–10, printed pp. [3]–6, complete mandate; dateline view 10
evidence.claim: The mandate describes its editorial programme and recipients and is dated 18 April 1740.

evidence.locus: view 11 Monitum; view 12 movable-feast table; view 280 printed p. 212; view 315 printed p. 245
evidence.claim: Marginal source sigla, a movable-feast table, a notated Advent preface and the Canon opening are present at these inspected loci; no complete wording is imported.

stages.limitations: The mandate describes changes relative to earlier practice, but no predecessor Évreux missal has been collated; no substantive transition, whole-book text or physical completeness is claimed. Printing year and mandate date are distinct events.
stages.reception: The mandate names diocesan churches, chapters, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities and confraternities, then priests bound by law or custom to the Évreux Office, and forbids other missals. This records the stated command and recipients, not actual uptake, a first effective date or later replacement.

stages.label: 1776 Lodève diocesan missal (Paris missal adopted with local adaptation)
stages.scope: The identified 1776 Lodève missal, its complete pastoral letter and the Canon opening.
stages.summary: The letter of Bishop Jean-Félix-Henri de Fumel says the old Lodève breviary had recently been restored, that only one copy of the old Lodève missal survived, and that, given the agreement found between the old Lodève and Paris breviaries, and presumed ('praesumpta') between the old missals of both churches, the Paris Missal was adopted ('Missale Parisiense duximus adoptandum'), with items removed from or added to the Proper of Time and the Proper and Common of Saints to suit Lodève practice and the rubrics adapted to local use. Proper Masses and prefaces are given to the solemnities and patronal feasts. The mandate commands diocesan churches, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities and priests bound to the Lodève Office to use this missal and no other.

evidence.claim: The book names Lodève, the bishop's authority with chapter consent, Paris, 1776 and the royal privilege.

evidence.locus: views 9–12, printed pp. 5–8; account of adoption view 11; mandate, dateline and Monitum view 12
evidence.claim: The letter states the adoption and adaptation of the Paris Missal and is dated 10 September 1775.
The Canon opens at this inspected page with a marginal Roman-sacramentary siglum.

stages.limitations: The letter's account of what was adopted and adapted is a primary description; no Paris missal or earlier Lodève missal has been collated with this book, so no transition is recorded. The 1775 letter and the 1776 printing are distinct events.
stages.reception: The mandate is addressed to the diocese's churches and rectors, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities and priests bound to the Lodève Office and forbids other missals. Actual uptake and duration of use are not established.

stages.label: 1543 Le Puy diocesan missal
stages.date_label: 1543 colophon (Lyon printing for a Le Puy bookseller)
stages.scope: The identified 1543 Le Puy missal at its title, Canon and colophon.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum Aniciensis ecclesiae, Lyon 1543, Lyon Rés 129080
stages.summary: A pre-Tridentine printing for the use of the church of Le Puy. The title promises chant and notes and newly added Masses; the colophon on f. CCCXII says Thibaud Payen printed it at Lyon in 1543 at the cost of Jean Allard, bookseller of Le Puy. The Canon is present; its opening reads 'pro nostris delictis et pro ecclesia' and names the bishop and king, observed here without collation.

evidence.claim: The book is titled a missal for the use of the church of Le Puy, sold at Le Puy by Jean Allard.

evidence.locus: view 673, f. CCCXII, colophon and register
evidence.claim: Printed at Lyon by Theobaldus Paganus for Jean Allard of Le Puy, 1543.
The Canon from Te igitur to Communicantes is present on this inspected page.

stages.limitations: No episcopal authority, calendar or proper sections were inspected; the commercial publication does not by itself establish episcopal approval. No predecessor or successor collation, transition or complete text is claimed; the observed Canon wording is not a collated variant claim.
stages.reception: Sale at Le Puy and the title's 'ad usum Aniciensis ecclesiae' attest intended local use, not actual adoption, approval or duration of use.

stages.label: 1831 Autun diocesan missal
stages.scope: The identified 1831 Autun missal, its episcopal mandate and the Canon opening.
stages.witness_label: Missale Aeduense, Autun 1831, Lyon copy (Google Books RxTk440szmAC)
stages.summary: The mandate of Bishop du Trousset d'Héricourt says that his predecessor's new breviary required a matching missal; the work, begun earlier and interrupted by death, reached him with errors and was completed by experts who conformed the missal to the general rubrics and the breviary, raised some Masses in rank, restored some and introduced new ones, and increased the cult of the Virgin, the Apostles and the bishops of Autun, Chalon and Mâcon. It orders the churches, rectors, confraternities, communities and priests bound to the Autun Office to use this missal, and no other, six months after the mandate's date.

evidence.claim: The book names Autun, the bishop's authority with chapter consent and 1831.

evidence.locus: PA3 printed p. 3, account of the work; PA6 printed p. 6, operative mandate and dateline
evidence.claim: The mandate describes the revision and is dated 30 December 1830, with use required six months later.
The Canon opens at this inspected page.

stages.limitations: The mandate's account is a primary description; neither the predecessor breviary nor an earlier missal has been collated. The mandate date, the six-month term and the printing year are distinct events; no transition or complete text is claimed.
stages.reception: The mandate is addressed to the churches, rectors, confraternities, communities and priests bound to the Autun Office. Actual uptake is not established; the 1856 return to the Roman liturgy (next stage) shows the book was later superseded.

stages.label: 1858 Autun proper Masses for the restored Roman liturgy
stages.date_label: 1858 printing; SRC decree of 17 April 1856 approving the calendar and proper; mandate of 11 May 1856
stages.scope: The identified 1858 Autun proper of Masses, its bishop's mandate restoring the Roman liturgy, the SRC letter and the printer's certification.
stages.witness_label: Missae ecclesiae Aeduensi propriae, Autun 1858, Lyon copy (Google Books hp2fFDt6djwC)
stages.summary: Bishop Frédéric de Marguerye's mandate of 11 May 1856 says that proper Masses and Offices of the three old dioceses of Autun, Chalon and Mâcon were composed according to the Roman rite with a calendar, examined by the Congregation of Rites and approved by Pius IX as a Roman-Autun calendar with proper Offices and Masses. It orders all clergy, from a day to be announced, to use only the Ritual, Ceremonial, Breviary and Missal of the Roman Church together with these approved propers, observing the Congregation's rubrics and decrees. Printed p. 3 carries two SRC acts, each with the bishop's concordat of 11 May 1856: a letter of 28 February 1856 granting privileges asked for the prompt resumption of the Roman liturgy in the diocese (among them continuing the custom of three consecutive Christmas night Masses), and the decree of 17 April 1856 approving the perpetual calendar and the proper of Offices and Masses, with the corrections noted, for perpetual observance in the Hours and in Masses. A certification dated 1 September 1858 attests that the printed proper agrees with the approved original.

evidence.claim: Proper Masses of the church of Autun approved by Pius IX and published by order of Bishop de Marguerye, Autun, 1858.

evidence.locus: PA1, printed p. 1, mandate and dateline
evidence.claim: The mandate prescribes the Roman Missal and other Roman books with the approved Autun propers and is dated 11 May 1856.

The SRC letter of 28 February 1856 grants privileges for the resumption of the Roman liturgy at Autun, and the SRC decree of 17 April 1856 approves the perpetual calendar and proper of Offices and Masses; both carry the concordat of 11 May 1856.

evidence.locus: PA5-IA1, certification heading (body read by OCR)
evidence.claim: The bishop certifies on 1 September 1858 that the printed proper agrees with the approved original.

stages.limitations: The Mass formularies were not examined individually and the Roman Missal edition used is not identified. The 1856 mandate left the effective day to a later announcement; no effective date is asserted. No transition from the 1831 missal is recorded because no Roman Missal text is in evidence here.
stages.reception: The mandate binds all clergy of the diocese from a day to be announced. The announcement and actual implementation are not established.

stages.label: 1765 Chalon-sur-Saône diocesan missal
stages.scope: The identified 1765 Chalon missal, its episcopal letter and mandate, and the Canon opening.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cabillonense, Paris 1765, Lyon copy (Google Books N1TiGewjnSIC)
stages.summary: Bishop Louis-Henri de Rochefort d'Ally's letter says that the new breviary recently published for the diocese required a missal arranged to correspond fully with its Offices. The mandate, on the advice of the cathedral chapter, orders the churches, deans, rectors, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities and priests bound to recite the Chalon Office to use this missal and no other.

evidence.claim: The book names Chalon, the bishop's authority with chapter consent, Paris, 1765 and the royal privilege.

evidence.locus: PP13, letter opening; PP17, printed p. 5, mandate and dateline
evidence.claim: The missal is conformed to the new breviary and mandated on 29 April 1765.
The Canon opens at this inspected page.

stages.limitations: The letter states the purpose of conformity to the breviary; no breviary or earlier missal is collated and no transition is claimed. The relation to the 1767 catalogue record is unresolved.
stages.reception: The mandate names diocesan institutions and priests bound to the Chalon Office. Actual uptake is not established; Chalon was suppressed in 1801 and its territory joined to Autun, whose 1856 mandate restored the Roman liturgy.

stages.label: 1753 Couserans diocesan missal
stages.scope: The identified 1753 Couserans missal, its complete letter and mandate, and the Canon opening.
stages.witness_label: Missale Conseranense, Paris 1753, BU Toulouse Res 1335
stages.summary: Bishop Joseph de Saint-André Marnais de Verceil's letter says the recently issued breviary required a matching missal. As his predecessor took antiphons and responsories of the breviary from Scripture, so the introits, graduals, offertories and communions of the missal are taken from Scripture. Nothing belonging to the norm of the Sacrifice observed in the whole Latin Church was changed, nothing new was introduced in the rites, and only a very few formerly frequent local usages were restored, keeping those customary to the diocese's priests and used by the Roman Church. All priests of the diocese are to use the new missal in private and solemn Masses and no other, except the Roman Missal in private Masses.

evidence.claim: The book names Couserans, the bishop's order and authority with chapter consent, Paris, 1753 and the royal privilege.
The letter describes the scriptural chant texts and limited ritual changes; the mandate of 12 July 1753 binds all priests, with an exception for the Roman Missal in private Masses.
The Canon opens at this inspected page.

stages.limitations: The letter's account is a primary description; no predecessor book or Roman Missal has been collated and no transition is claimed.
stages.reception: The mandate binds all priests of the diocese in private and solemn Masses and expressly tolerates the Roman Missal in private Masses. Actual uptake is not established; Couserans was suppressed in 1801.

stages.label: 1766 Albi diocesan missal
stages.scope: The identified 1766 Albi missal, the inspected part of its letter and mandate, and the Canon opening.
stages.witness_label: Missale Albiense, Paris 1766, BU Toulouse Res 1341
stages.summary: Archbishop Léopold-Charles de Choiseul's letter says prefaces were added where proper ones were lacking (Advent, Corpus Christi, Dedication, All Saints and others), following the ancient Roman custom still kept in the Ambrosian rite; most collects, secrets and postcommunions were taken from ancient sacramentaries, including the Leonine Sacramentary published at the Vatican under Clement XII, with very few new prayers modelled on them, and slight verbal changes were allowed without altering doctrine. The mandate orders the churches, deans, rectors, orders, colleges, monasteries, communities and priests bound to the Albi Office to use this missal and no other, and forbids printers to reprint the old missals.

evidence.claim: The book names Albi, the archbishop's authority with chapter consent, Paris, 1766 and the royal privilege.

evidence.locus: images 14–16, printed pp. 6–8, letter, mandate and dateline
evidence.claim: The letter describes added prefaces and sacramentary sources; the mandate is dated 2 January 1763.
The Canon opens at this inspected page.

stages.limitations: The letter's account is a primary description; no predecessor missal is collated and no transition is claimed. The 1763 letter, the 1764 catalogue record and this 1766 printing are distinct; whether 1766 reprints a 1764 first printing is unresolved.
stages.reception: The mandate names diocesan institutions and priests bound to the Albi Office and forbids reprinting old missals. Actual uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1891 Luçon proper Masses for use with the Roman Missal
stages.scope: The identified 1891 Luçon proper of Masses, its approval decree and first proper page.
stages.witness_label: Missae propriae ad usum ecclesiae Lucionensis, 1891, Harvard copy (Google Books t-wtAAAAYAAJ)
stages.summary: At the request of Bishop Clovis Catteau, Leo XIII approved on 9 July 1890, on the report of the Congregation of Rites, emendations and additions to the Calendar and Proper for the clergy of Luçon. The proper of Masses was published by the episcopal chancery in 1891 and printed by Pustet at Regensburg; its rubrics refer to the general rubrics of the Roman Missal, so it supplements the Roman Missal rather than replacing it.

evidence.claim: Proper Masses for the church of Luçon approved by Leo XIII and edited by order of Bishop Clovis, 1891, printed at Regensburg.
The SRC approval is dated 9 July 1890; concordat 21 March 1891; imprimatur 24 March 1891.
The first proper Mass carries a rubric referring to the general rubrics of the Roman Missal.

stages.limitations: The date when Luçon adopted the Roman Missal is not stated in the inspected pages. The Mass formularies were not examined individually; no transition from the 1766/1767 or 1828 diocesan missals is claimed.
stages.reception: The decree concerns the clergy of the diocese of Luçon. Actual use is not established beyond the publication.

stages.label: Roman Missal imposed in the diocese of Elne from 1 January 1848
stages.date_label: Mandate of 1 November 1847, effective from 'the next 1 January' (1 January 1848)
stages.scope: The mandated replacement of every other missal by the Roman Missal with a diocesan proper in the diocese of Elne (Perpignan), as stated in the inspected mandate.
stages.witness_label: Mandate printed in Officia propria ad usum dioecesis Elnensis, Perpignan 1847 (Google Books Hc4-AAAAYAAJ)
stages.summary: Bishop Jean-François of Elne ordered on 1 November 1847 that, from the following 1 January, all clergy use the Roman Missal and Breviary with the diocesan proper he had arranged, in solemn and private celebration, and declared every other missal or breviary prohibited after that date.

evidence.locus: PR7–PR8, printed pp. vii–viii, operative mandate and dateline
evidence.claim: The mandate imposes the Roman Missal and Breviary with the proper from 1 January following and prohibits other missals; dated 1 November 1847.

stages.limitations: This records a mandated change of Mass book, not an inspected Roman Missal or a printed Mass proper; no edition, text or actual compliance is established. Effective date is the one the mandate sets; it is not an observed first use. The mandate says 'a calendis januarii proxime occurrentis'; the year 1848 is computed from its 1 November 1847 dateline. The proper it names ('hoc proprio') is the Officia propria in which it is printed; whether that book contains Mass formularies is not established.
stages.reception: The mandate is addressed to all the diocese's archdeacons, canons, archpriests, deans, parish priests, vicars, priests and clerics in sacred orders. Compliance is not established.

stages.label: 1857 approved Angers proper of Masses for the Roman liturgy
stages.scope: The SRC approval of the Angers perpetual calendar and proper of Offices and Masses, to be observed in Masses, as reprinted and inspected.
stages.witness_label: SRC decree reprinted in Officia propria Andegavensis, 1881 (Google Books tf6MPdwy1g0C)
stages.summary: On 17 June 1857 the Congregation of Rites approved, with marginal corrections, the perpetual calendar and the proper of Offices and Masses of the diocese of Angers, to be observed perpetually by its clergy in the Hours according to the Roman rite and in the celebration of Masses. The decree's narrative places this within Bishop Guillaume-Laurent-Louis Angebault's recall of the Roman liturgy to his diocese.

evidence.claim: Bishop Angebault, seeking to recall the Roman liturgy to his diocese, submitted a perpetual calendar and proper of Offices and Masses to Pius IX.

evidence.locus: PT8, printed p. 50, operative clause, dateline and concordat
evidence.claim: The approval of the Angers calendar and proper of Offices and Masses for observance in Masses is dated 17 June 1857.

stages.limitations: The approved proper's Mass texts and the Roman Missal edition are not inspected; the reprint is in an 1881 office book. Approval date is not an effective or first-use date.
stages.reception: The decree grants perpetual observance by the clergy of Angers. Implementation is not established.

stages.label: 1543/1544 Bayonne diocesan missal of Bishop Étienne Poncher
stages.date_label: Title 1543; printing completed January 1544 new style (Dubarat p. lxxxix gives 28 January twice and 24 January once)
stages.scope: The 1543/1544 Bayonne missal as described by Dubarat from the Mazarine copy: title, physical make-up, calendar, temporale, Ordinary with notated prefaces, Canon and sanctoral.
stages.witness_label: Missale ... Bajocensis [Bayonne], Paris 1543/1544, Mazarine 1162 B, as described by Dubarat 1891
stages.summary: Dubarat, following P. Marais, restores to Bayonne a Paris missal of 1543 (finished in January 1544 new style; he gives both 28 and 24 January) whose title misprints 'Bajocensis' for Bayonne: folio 1 reads 'secundum usum ecclesie diocesis Bajon.', the arms and order are those of Étienne Poncher, bishop of Bayonne, and the title calls the book carefully emended, enlarged and revised. He describes a calendar, blessings including one for ships, a temporale for the diocese of Bayonne, notated prefaces including a proper Palm Sunday preface, a Canon with added passages, and a sanctoral, common and votive Masses in a second part.

evidence.claim: The volume titled 'Bajocensis' is the Bayonne missal printed by order of Étienne Poncher, finished in January 1544 new style (28 January, and 24 January in Marais's quoted conclusion); Mazarine 1162 B is the only known copy.
Transcribed title, printer and date, and physical description.
Contents: calendar, temporale incipit for the diocese of Bayonne, notated prefaces, Canon with additions, sanctoral, common and votive Masses.

stages.limitations: Documented from an inspected scholarly description with exact loci, not from the original; Dubarat's characterization of the Canon additions as Gallican is his judgment. No collation, transition or complete text is claimed.
stages.reception: The title states episcopal order for the cathedral church of Bayonne. Actual diocesan use and duration are not established.
